To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the models developed using statistical relational learning algorithms are as good as or better than current handcrafted rules, (b) the models are easy to interpret, and (c) the models incorporate relational information in ways not possible before now.

relational knowledge discovery can help NASD focus its regulatory resources more effectively, and can do so with models that are competitive with those developed using traditional data mining techniques.
relational machine learning models can predict securities violations better than the current state-of-the-art at NASD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing new computational techniques for analyzing large-scale relational data, which is increasingly common in many application areas.
developing and testing a new approach to a real-world problem of great importance.
the application of machine learning algorithms to a real-world problem of great societal importance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed a model that can be used to help focus regulatory resources in a manner that is more effective than the current approach.
the statistical relational learning approach was successful in this application, and that the approach has potential for broader use in the financial services sector.

we have developed a new method that is at least as accurate as the best current methods, and that is more accurate than some of the current methods, and is more accurate than the current methods in the cases where the current methods have been shown to be inaccurate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the statistical relational learning algorithms we developed are able to learn models that are competitive with the handcrafted models used in practice.
we have demonstrated that relational knowledge discovery is an effective and practical way to support a key regulatory task.

we were able to improve NASD's ability to identify brokers who are at high risk of committing a securities violation by using statistical relational learning algorithms that incorporate the organizational relationships among brokers.
The main takeaway from our work is that

relational knowledge discovery is now sufficiently mature to enable the discovery of new, useful knowledge in complex domains, even when the data is noisy, the number of attributes is large, and the domain is highly dynamic.
statistical relational learning can be applied successfully to a real-world problem in which the data are complex and noisy, and the domain experts are not statisticians.
statistical relational learning algorithms are a powerful new tool for the domain of securities regulation.
